Focus is on literature detailing constant residual correction methods, particularly scalar offsets. The core issue is the consistent omission of a constant (3) by the fixed predictor 2x within the given data. Need to ascertain if existing works provide a framework for explaining this discrepancy without implying novel methodological contributions beyond observed calculations or implying a general research problem.

Literature suggests recalibration techniques can address the fixed predictor's systematic bias. Specifically, updating the intercept (offset) of a model aligns with the observed need to correct the constant residual. Examining papers on regression through the origin clarifies how omitting an intercept term results in non-zero mean residuals, and adding one addresses this systematic error. Platt (1999) and Guo et al. (2017) provide further frameworks on fitting scalar adjustments to fixed outputs.

The task involves identifying 10 to 15 relevant papers.

Clements & Hendry (1996) provides the theoretical basis for intercept correction in forecasting. Turner (1990) explores macroeconomic forecasting, where intercept corrections are applied based on residual monitoring. Steyerberg et al. (2004) explains intercept-only adjustment to restore calibration when there are baseline offsets.

Identified additional papers demonstrating intercept adjustment's effectiveness. Vergouwe et al. (2017) presents a testing procedure to determine when a simple intercept adjustment suffices. Eisenhauer (2003) and Casella (1983) explain how omitting the intercept leads to constant mean residuals, confirming the need for correction when an intercept is present.

Demonstrated intercept correction effectiveness in nowcasting location shifts, as constant residual biases are corrected by indicator saturation. Post-hoc calibration methods, including vector scaling and affine calibration with intercept offsets, are effective for adjusting output distributions through scalar corrections on frozen base predictor logits. Affine transformation with intercept offset and slope further validates the resolution of calibration errors.

Confirmed that the identified papers meet the specified count criteria. These papers explore intercept corrections within broader frameworks. The reasoning considered stagewise additive corrections to residuals, focusing on distribution-free predictive inference and forecasting with structural breaks.
